title: TS SDK: Multiplexing streaming façade with abort tokens and graceful shutdown
creator: Ava Patel
description:
Purpose: Provide a single, ergonomic TypeScript SDK surface that lets applications consume streaming LLM responses as either AsyncIterable or Web Streams while enabling safe consumer multiplexing, explicit checkpoints, and clear abort/cancellation semantics that map to runtime resources.

Background: Current SDK helpers focus on single-consumer patterns and several teams have implemented custom adapters to support handoff between AsyncIterator and ReadableStream consumers. This causes subtle bugs around cancellation (resource leaks, dangling KV cache entries) and poor developer ergonomics when multiple layers need to observe or re-consume a stream.

Scope: Implement a streaming façade (StreamFacade) and runtime contract that exposes: (1) asAsyncIterable(response): AsyncIterable<StreamChunk>, (2) asWebReadable(response): ReadableStream<StreamChunk>, (3) checkpoint(resumeHandle): opaque token that can be attached to a subsequent request to resume from a prefix or cached KV-state, (4) finish/abort methods that deterministically free runtime resources and emit terminal events to all consumers, (5) multiplex API to allow n logical consumers to attach with isolation (each receives same sequence but can pause/resume independently without impacting runtime batching). Deliver samples for Node (native streams), Deno, and Browser (fetch + Streams API).

Non-goal: Implementing server-side cross-request resumability (beyond providing an opaque resume token) or complex application-level merging logic for partial consumers.

Compatibility notes: The façade must not change existing synchronous generation API. It should interoperate with existing TS SDK types and be tree-shakeable for browser bundles.
acceptance_criteria: Public TS API exported as StreamFacade with helpers asAsyncIterable and asWebReadable
Multiplexing: at least two independent consumer attach points that do not cancel runtime when one consumer aborts
Abort semantics: abort() (or any consumer's AbortSignal) triggers deterministic runtime resource cleanup and a single terminal error event to all consumers
Checkpoint tokens: produce opaque string tokens that can be passed to subsequent requests and are validated by runtime for compatible model/seq-length
Examples: working samples for Node, Deno, and Browser demonstrating adapter usage and resume with checkpoint
Automated tests covering cancel propagation, multiplex pause/resume, and perf regression benchmarks (CI gating)
tasks: Write design doc and compatibility matrix (link in attachments)
Add StreamFacade types and runtime hooks in ts-sdk core
Implement demultiplexer with weak-ref consumer bookkeeping and deterministic cleanup
Wire AbortSignal propagation from consumer -> facade -> runtime (and backpressure semantics)
Expose helper conversions: ReadableStream <-> AsyncIterable adapters with minimal copying
Add resume token generation + server-side validation spec and client examples
Integration tests (node, deno, browser harness) and CI steps
Docs: migration guide, example snippets, and changelog entry for sdk-2026.03
comments: 2026-03-10 - Ava Patel: Created ticket after RFC review. Initial design doc uploaded to Confluence.

2026-03-11 - Mateo Chen: Spike completed for multiplexing prototype (branch: feature/stream-facade-spike). Observed 8% p95 regression when naive fanout without shared buffer. Need shared chunk buffer with refcounts.
2026-03-12 - Design review (Sofia Martinez): Requested clearer semantic for checkpoint tokens (must include model id + prefix hash). Also asked to avoid leaking internal KV keys in token format.

2026-03-13 - Mateo Chen: Implemented AbortSignal chaining and initial adapter tests. Added two new CI matrices: node-18, deno-1.28. Opened PR for early feedback: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/4123
2026-03-14 - PM review (Noah Green): Prioritized this as P1 for 2026.03 release due to multiple customer issues around stream cancellation. Confirmed no blocking legal requirements.
notes: Trade-offs: copying vs shared buffer. We favor a shared (immutable) chunk buffer with shallow refs to avoid tokenization/rehydration costs. Consumers will receive read-only chunk objects to avoid accidental mutation.
Testing plan: End-to-end harness will spawn a small runtime docker instance that simulates partial token emission and validates resume semantics using test resume tokens.
Observability: wire span events for 'stream.open', 'stream.checkpoint', 'stream.abort', and 'stream.close' so Console can surface per-route streaming metrics and token usage counts.
